+---
+title: Claude Code Integration Guide
+author: CubeSandbox contributors
+date: 2026-07-02
+tags:
+  - integration
+  - claude-code
+  - coding-agent
+lang: en-US
+---
+
+# Claude Code Integration Guide
+
+This guide shows how to run Claude Code inside CubeSandbox so terminal-based coding work happens in an isolated, reproducible sandbox. The same pattern also works when an external agent orchestrator creates CubeSandbox sandboxes on demand and asks Claude Code to inspect or modify files through the sandbox process API.
+
+The runnable example is under `examples/claude-code-integration/`.
+
+## Integration Target and Version
+
+- Target: Claude Code, Anthropic's terminal coding agent.
+- Tested installation path: `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.198`.
+- Runtime: Node.js, npm, Git, ripgrep, and a Cube base image with envd on port `49983`.
+- Default user: non-root `cubesandbox`, with `/workspace` writable by that user.
+- CubeSandbox API: E2B-compatible Python SDK path via `cubesandbox`.
+
+Claude Code is an interactive CLI. The example keeps the default validation non-interactive: it verifies `claude --version`, prepares a Git workspace, snapshots the sandbox, restores from that snapshot, and optionally runs a real Claude prompt when `RUN_CLAUDE_PROMPT=1` is set.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A running CubeSandbox cluster and `cubemastercli` configured for it.
+- Docker access on the build machine.
+- A registry reachable by every Cubelet when running a multi-node cluster.
+- Python 3.10+ for the example runner.
+- Optional Anthropic credential:
+  - `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for direct API access.
+  - `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` if your Claude Code setup uses token-based auth.
+  - `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` if traffic goes through an Anthropic-compatible gateway.
+
+## Build the Claude Code Template
+
+The example image installs Claude Code into a Cube base image:
+
+```bash
+cd examples/claude-code-integration
+REGISTRY_IMAGE=<your-registry>/cubesandbox-claude-code:latest ./build_template.sh
+```
+
+For single-node local deployments, `REGISTRY_IMAGE` can be omitted if the Cubelet can see the local Docker image. For multi-node deployments, push the image to a registry first so every node can pull it.
+
+The script registers the image with:
+
+```bash
+cubemastercli tpl create-from-image \
+  --image <image> \
+  --writable-layer-size 4G \
+  --expose-port 49983 \
+  --probe 49983 \
+  --probe-path /health
+```
+
+Record the printed template ID.
+
+## Configure Credentials and Cube Access
+
+Copy the environment template:
+
+```bash
+cp examples/claude-code-integration/env.example examples/claude-code-integration/.env
+```
+
+Set the required CubeSandbox values:
+
+```bash
+CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID=tpl-...
+E2B_API_URL=http://<cube-api-host>:3000
+E2B_API_KEY=e2b_000000
+```
+
+For direct Claude Code calls, add:
+
+```bash
+ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
+# ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=...
+ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.anthropic.com
+```
+
+There are two safe ways to handle sensitive values:
+
+- **SDK env injection**: pass credentials through `Sandbox.create(env_vars=...)`. This is simple and works well for local examples, but the secret is visible to processes inside the sandbox.
+- **CubeEgress credential injection**: configure a CubeEgress rule that injects the outbound `Authorization` header for Anthropic or your gateway. This keeps the raw secret outside the sandbox filesystem and process environment. Use this for shared or multi-tenant deployments.
+
+## Run the Example
+
+```bash
+cd examples/claude-code-integration
+pip install -r requirements.txt
+python3 run_claude_code.py
+```
+
+Expected output:
+
+```text
+claude version: ...
+skipping real Claude API call ...
+snapshot: snap-...
+restored file: hello from CubeSandbox
+snapshot deleted
+```

+---
+title: Claude Code 集成指南
+author: CubeSandbox contributors
+date: 2026-07-02
+tags:
+  - integration
+  - claude-code
+  - coding-agent
+lang: zh-CN
+---
+
+# Claude Code 集成指南
+
+本文说明如何把 Claude Code 运行在 CubeSandbox 中，让终端型编码 Agent 的文件编辑、命令执行、依赖安装和测试运行都发生在隔离、可复现的沙箱内。同一模式也适用于外部 Agent 编排系统：编排系统按需创建 CubeSandbox 沙箱，再让 Claude Code 通过沙箱 process API 检查或修改文件。
+
+可运行示例位于 `examples/claude-code-integration/`。
+
+## 集成对象与版本
+
+- 集成对象：Claude Code，Anthropic 的终端编码 Agent。
+- 安装方式：`npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.198`。
+- 运行环境：Node.js、npm、Git、ripgrep，以及在 `49983` 端口运行 envd 的 Cube base image。
+- 默认用户：非 root `cubesandbox`，并且 `/workspace` 对该用户可写。
+- CubeSandbox API：通过 `cubesandbox` 使用 E2B 兼容的 Python SDK 路径。
+
+Claude Code 是交互式 CLI。示例默认采用非交互验证：检查 `claude --version`，准备 Git 工作区，创建沙箱快照，从快照恢复，并在设置 `RUN_CLAUDE_PROMPT=1` 时可选执行真实 Claude prompt。
+
+## 前置条件
+
+- 已部署 CubeSandbox 集群，并配置好 `cubemastercli`。
+- 构建机器可以使用 Docker。
+- 多节点集群需要一个所有 Cubelet 都能访问的镜像仓库。
+- 示例 runner 需要 Python 3.10+。
+- 可选 Anthropic 凭证：
+  - 直连 API 使用 `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`。
+  - 如果你的 Claude Code 配置使用 token 鉴权，可使用 `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`。
+  - 通过 Anthropic 兼容网关访问时，设置 `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`。
+
+## 构建 Claude Code 模板
+
+示例镜像会把 Claude Code 安装到 Cube base image 中：
+
+```bash
+cd examples/claude-code-integration
+REGISTRY_IMAGE=<your-registry>/cubesandbox-claude-code:latest ./build_template.sh
+```
+
+单节点本地部署时，如果 Cubelet 能看到本地 Docker 镜像，可以不设置 `REGISTRY_IMAGE`。多节点部署时，请先推送镜像到所有节点可拉取的仓库。
+
+脚本会用以下配置注册模板：
+
+```bash
+cubemastercli tpl create-from-image \
+  --image <image> \
+  --writable-layer-size 4G \
+  --expose-port 49983 \
+  --probe 49983 \
+  --probe-path /health
+```
+
+记录输出的 template ID。
+
+## 配置凭证与 Cube 访问
+
+复制环境变量模板：
+
+```bash
+cp examples/claude-code-integration/env.example examples/claude-code-integration/.env
+```
+
+设置必填 CubeSandbox 参数：
+
+```bash
+CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID=tpl-...
+E2B_API_URL=http://<cube-api-host>:3000
+E2B_API_KEY=e2b_000000
+```
+
+如需真实调用 Claude Code，增加：
+
+```bash
+ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
+# ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=...
+ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.anthropic.com
+```
+
+敏感配置有两种推荐注入方式：
+
+- **SDK 环境变量注入**：通过 `Sandbox.create(env_vars=...)` 传入凭证。适合本地示例，配置简单，但密钥会对沙箱内进程可见。
+- **CubeEgress 凭证注入**：配置 CubeEgress 规则，在访问 Anthropic 或你的网关时注入出站 `Authorization` header。这样原始密钥不会出现在沙箱文件系统或进程环境中，适合共享或多租户部署。
+
+## 运行示例
+
+```bash
+cd examples/claude-code-integration
+pip install -r requirements.txt
+python3 run_claude_code.py
+```
+
+预期输出：
+
+```text
+claude version: ...
+skipping real Claude API call ...
+snapshot: snap-...
+restored file: hello from CubeSandbox
+snapshot deleted
+```
+
+执行真实 prompt：
+
+```bash
+RUN_CLAUDE_PROMPT=1 python3 run_claude_code.py
+```
+
+真实 prompt 路径需要 `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` 或 `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`。
+
+## 网络与出口策略
+
+Claude Code 运行时需要出站 HTTPS 访问 Anthropic 或你配置的网关。模板构建阶段也需要访问 npm registry，除非你使用内部镜像源。
+
+开放式开发沙箱可使用默认配置：
+
+```python
+Sandbox.create(template=template_id, allow_internet_access=True)
+```
+
+如需限制运行时出口，可在示例中设置 `STRICT_EGRESS=1`。脚本会使用 `allow_internet_access=False` 和域名白名单创建沙箱：
+
+```python
+Sandbox.create(
+    template=template_id,
+    allow_internet_access=False,
+    network={
+        "allow_out": [
+            "api.anthropic.com",
+            "console.anthropic.com",
+            "registry.npmjs.org",
+            "github.com",
+            "raw.githubusercontent.com",
+        ],
+    },
+)
+```
+
+如果使用私有 LLM 网关，请放通该网关域名，替代或补充 `api.anthropic.com`。如果需要请求级过滤、审计或 header 注入，请按 Security Proxy 文档配置 CubeEgress `rules`。
+
+## 会话保持与状态持久化
+
+使用 CubeSandbox 快照保存 Claude Code 状态：
+
+1. 在 `/workspace` 中运行 Claude Code。
+2. 将源码、`.git`、任务笔记和生成产物保存在 `/workspace`。
+3. 在合适检查点调用 `sandbox.create_snapshot()`。
+4. 后续用 `Sandbox.create(template=snapshot_id)` 恢复。
+
+示例镜像默认以非 root `cubesandbox` 用户运行。如果你的编排层覆盖了进程用户，请确保 `/workspace` 的属主与运行用户一致。
+
+示例使用如下流程：
+
+```python
+snapshot = sandbox.create_snapshot(name="claude-code-smoke")
+snapshot_id = snapshot.snapshot_id
+
+with Sandbox.create(template=snapshot_id) as restored:
+    restored.commands.run("python3 /workspace/hello.py")
+```
+
+如果只是短时间挂起，可以使用 `sandbox.pause()` 和 `Sandbox.connect(sandbox_id)` 保留沙箱会话。若状态需要长时间存在，或需要克隆到多个后续沙箱，应使用快照。
+
+## 典型使用场景
+
+- **隔离运行编码 Agent**：把 Claude Code 本身放进 CubeSandbox，让文件修改、依赖安装、测试运行和生成产物都留在沙箱内。
+- **执行 Agent 生成代码**：Claude Code 或其他编排器运行在沙箱外，只把不可信命令放到 CubeSandbox 中执行并回收结果。
+- **长任务断点续跑**：在依赖安装、仓库 checkout、测试基线通过后创建快照，中断后从最后一个可用快照恢复。
+- **并行探索**：从准备好的仓库创建一个快照，再克隆多个沙箱测试不同 Claude Code prompt 或分支。
+
+## 注意事项
+
+- Claude Code CLI 参数可能随版本变化。示例通过 Docker build 参数 `CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION` 固定 `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` 版本；升级 CLI 时应显式修改并重新验证。
+- Dockerfile 在添加 Node.js apt 源之前会校验 NodeSource 签名 key 的 fingerprint。如果 NodeSource 轮换 key，请先通过独立渠道确认新 key，再更新 `NODESOURCE_KEY_FINGERPRINT`。
+- 交互式终端体验取决于你的编排层。示例使用非交互 process 调用，便于在 CI 和本地部署中验证。
+- 域名白名单依赖 DNS 学习。使用域名 `allow_out` 时，应设置 `allow_internet_access=False` 或提供 deny-all fallback，避免未匹配公网流量默认放行。
+- 以环境变量注入的密钥会对沙箱内进程可见。共享基础设施建议使用 CubeEgress 注入。
+
+## 常见问题
+
+| 现象 | 常见原因 | 处理方式 |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `claude: command not found` | 模板未基于 Claude Code 镜像构建，或 npm 安装失败 | 重新构建镜像并重新创建模板 |
+| `Template not found` | `CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID` 错误，或连接了错误集群 | 检查 `cubemastercli tpl list` |
+| 鉴权失败 | 缺少或错误的 Anthropic 凭证 | 设置 `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`、`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`，或配置 CubeEgress 注入 |
+| 网络超时 | 出站策略阻止了 LLM 端点 | 将网关域名加入 `allow_out`，或调试时关闭严格出口策略 |
+| HTTPS 证书错误 | 模板不信任 CubeEgress CA | 基于带 CA 的 Cube base image 构建，或配置正确 CA 路径 |
+| 镜像拉取失败 | Cubelet 无法拉取模板镜像 | 推送到所有节点可访问的镜像仓库并重新创建模板 |
+| 快照恢复后缺少状态 | 文件在快照之后写入，或写到了沙箱文件系统外 | 在 `create_snapshot()` 前写入状态，并把项目文件放在 `/workspace` |
+
+## 参考
+
+- 示例：`examples/claude-code-integration/`

**Health probe will always fail — no service listens on port 49983**

The template registers a health probe on port 49983 at `/health`, but no process in the image serves this endpoint. The Cubelet's health checks will always get connection refused, which may cause restart loops or false failure reports.

Either:
- Add a minimal HTTP server that responds `200 OK` on `/health` (e.g., a simple Python one-liner or `nc`-based listener), or
- Remove `--probe` and `--probe-path` from this command and add a comment noting when and how to add health checks.

review_comments.body:
**Redundant RUN layer & unnecessary runtime package**

Two issues in the Dockerfile:

1. **Redundant `RUN chown` (this line):** The `chown -R` on line 45 already sets ownership of `/workspace/README.md`. This separate `RUN` layer adds unnecessary image metadata and slows push/pull. Merge it into the preceding `RUN` or remove it entirely.

2. **`jq` installed in final image:** `jq` on line 24 is only used during the key-fingerprint verification pipeline (gpg key parsing). It is never needed at runtime, adding ~2MB to the writable layer that CubeSandbox must snapshot. Either move it to a separate build stage, or replace the `awk | grep` pipeline with a pure-gpg approach and remove `jq` from the install list.

**`E2B_API_KEY` is validated but never consumed by the SDK**

The required-env check mandates `E2B_API_KEY` (line 30), but the `cubesandbox` Python SDK does not actually read this variable or send any authentication header. This creates a misleading sense of security — a user who omits the key still passes validation, and a user who sets it may believe the connection is authenticated when it isn't.

Either remove `E2B_API_KEY` from the required check, or add the auth header to the SDK calls.

**`allow_internet_access=False` may override the allowlist**

When `STRICT_EGRESS=1`, both `allow_internet_access=False` and `network={"allow_out": [...]}` are passed to `Sandbox.create()`. The semantics of combining these two flags may be ambiguous — if the SDK treats `allow_internet_access=False` as a blanket deny, the `allow_out` list becomes a no-op.

Please verify the SDK's behavior: does `allow_internet_access=False` + `network.allow_out` work as intended, or should `allow_internet_access` be omitted when providing a custom network config?

review_comments.body:
**Probe path may fail — no HTTP endpoint at `/health`**

The `--probe-path /health` flag tells CubeSandbox to perform an HTTP GET on `/health`, but the image does not serve any HTTP endpoint at that path (the base image's envd does serve port 49983, but not necessarily with a `/health` handler accessible via this probe path). If CubeSandbox performs an HTTP-level check rather than a TCP socket check, this probe will always fail.

Either confirm that the probe is a TCP-only check (and remove `--probe-path`), or ensure the image serves a health endpoint at `/health`.

## Review: PR #710 — LangGraph + CubeSandbox Example

Overall this is a well-structured example with clean module separation, proper cleanup (`finally` + `sandbox.kill()`), correct SSL isolation via `certifi` + `trust_env=False`, and thorough documentation. A few issues worth addressing:

### Bugs & Runtime Issues

- **demo_common.py:82** — `messages[-1]` on an empty list raises `IndexError`. The `if messages` guard is truthy for `[]`. Use an explicit `len()` check.
- **env_utils.py:32-35** — If `CUBE_SSL_CERT_FILE` is set but the file doesn't exist, the code silently does nothing. The TLS handshake then fails with a cryptic error. Print a warning when the path is missing.

### Correctness

- **llm_utils.py:17-18** — Splitting on `:` without validation silently corrupts model names with colons (e.g., `ft:gpt-4o:org:2024-01-01` → `2024-01-01`). Document the expected format or validate it.
- **llm_utils.py:21** — `httpx.Client` is created but never closed. For a one-shot demo script this is harmless, but it's a connection-pool leak if reused. Consider wrapping with a context manager.

### Design

- **demo_common.py:32,59** — Both `run_sandbox_check()` and `run_agent_demo()` accept an unused `sandbox` parameter. Either remove it or add a `# keep ref for GC` comment and make the intent clear.
- **e2b_demo.py:21** — `apply_cube_envd_patches()` is called at import time, which makes the module impossible to import for testing without triggering real SDK mutations. Guarding behind `if __name__ == "__main__"` would improve testability.

### Security

- **`.env.example`** defaults to `http://` for `E2B_API_URL`. An attacker on the same network segment can intercept the API key and sandbox traffic. Recommend defaulting to HTTPS and documenting the TLS setup.
- **`env_utils.py:31`** — `SSL_CERT_FILE` is set from user-controlled input with only an `os.path.isfile()` guard. Consider validating the file is a parseable PEM certificate before trusting it.

### Documentation

- Both READMEs' "CubeSandbox adaptations" table lists `workdir` and `CUBE_SSL_CERT_FILE` as patches in `cube_patches.py`, but they're actually in `demo_common.py` and `env_utils.py` respectively. Move those rows out of the patch table or add file annotations.

### Positive Highlights

- Clean separation of concerns across 5 modules
- Idempotent patching with `_PATCHED` guard
- Proper `finally`-based sandbox cleanup
- Correct SSL isolation between sandbox and LLM traffic
- Well-documented version pinning in requirements.txt

## Overview

This PR adds optional route-aware egress for sandbox outbound traffic by injecting packets into a `cube-router` dummy device, letting the Linux kernel routing stack decide the real egress NIC. The architecture is sound — the `from_world` BPF program sharing between primary NIC ingress and cube-router egress is reasonable, and the default behavioral compatibility is preserved when cube-router is disabled.

## Code Quality

1. **Resource leak in `getOrCreateCubeRouter` device creation path** (`network-agent/internal/service/cube_router.go:228`). When the cube-router dummy device does not yet exist and `LinkAdd` succeeds but a subsequent call (`AddrAdd`, `LinkSetUp`, `LinkSetMTU`) fails, the orphaned device is never cleaned up. The existing-link path (lines 153-207) is safe because it operates on a known-existing device, but the creation path needs deferred cleanup.

2. **`rewriteConstants` mixed nil-guard pattern** (`CubeNet/cubevs/miscs.go:44`). The new egress variables are nil-guarded (good), but the existing nodenic/nodegw specs at lines 59-64 are not — they would panic on a nil `*ebpf.VariableSpec`. Either guard all or none.

3. **Shell code duplication** (`deploy/one-click/lib/common.sh`). The `_check_cidr_conflict` function repeats the same CIDR range computation (~7 lines of bit-twiddling) three times independently, each with different variable prefixes. The `patch_cubelet_config_template` function adds 15-20 lines per config field with an identical grep/sed/grep pattern. Both would benefit from reusable helpers.

## Security

4. **Global `ip_forward` without FORWARD chain baseline** (`network-agent/internal/service/cube_router.go:419`). Enabling `ip_forward` globally applies to all interfaces. If the system's FORWARD default policy is ACCEPT, the node could forward arbitrary inter-interface traffic. Consider setting `-P FORWARD DROP` as baseline before adding the specific cube-router ACCEPT rules.

5. **Host ephemeral port range narrowed** (`network-agent/internal/service/local_service.go:178`). The host gets 10000-19999 (10K ports), down from the default ~28K, while sandbox SNAT gets 30000-65535 (~35K). Under high concurrency, host-side components (coredns, OpenResty, CubeMaster) could exhaust ports before sandbox SNAT does. Consider documenting or redistributing.

## Performance

6. **Extra forwarding hop is the key trade-off** (`network-agent/internal/service/cube_router.go`, `CubeNet/src/mvmtap.bpf.c`). Route-aware egress adds an estimated 3-15 µs per-packet latency due to kernel routing stack traversal (FIB lookup, conntrack, FORWARD chain). This is inherent to the design. The BPF-level changes (global `egress_redirect_flags` reads, L2 MAC source change, ifindex guard) all add negligible overhead. Direct mode remains available for latency-sensitive workloads.

## Documentation

7. **Verify iptables command ambiguous** (`docs/guide/route-aware-egress.md:78`). `iptables -t nat -S POSTROUTING | grep MASQUERADE` returns all MASQUERADE rules with no way to distinguish cube-router entries. Consider `grep -E 'MASQUERADE.*! -o cube-router'` instead.

8. **`CUBE_SANDBOX_CUBE_ROUTER_CIDR` silently ignored when ENABLE=0** (`deploy/one-click/env.example:140`). The install script only evaluates the CIDR when both ENABLE=1 and the CIDR is non-empty. If set without enable, it's silently ignored. The env.example comment should note this dependency.

## Test Coverage

9. **`cube_router.go` lacks unit tests** (`network-agent/internal/service/cube_router.go`, 646 lines). The file declares `netlinkAddrList`, `netlinkRouteDel`, and `execCommand` override variables (lines 22-26) that are clearly intended for test injection, but no test file exercises them. The pure-logic derivation functions (`deriveCubeRouterCIDRSpec`, `deriveCubeRouterSpecFromSandboxCIDR`) and iptables helpers have no direct test coverage beyond what the existing tests achieve incidentally.

10. **No integration/e2e tests for the cube-router egress path**. The eBPF changes, the conditional `NewLocalService` branch, and the `CubeRouterIfindex != 0` attachment path in `miscs.go:268` all lack automated verification.

## Summary

Add optional route-aware egress for sandbox outbound traffic.

When enabled, CubeVS sends sandbox outbound packets into an internal `cube-router` device instead of always redirecting them to the node primary NIC. The Linux routing stack then decides the real egress device, so sandbox traffic can follow host routes through physical NICs, GRE/VXLAN tunnels, VPN devices, or other routable interfaces.

## What changed

- Add optional `cube-router` based egress path.
- Keep the original primary-NIC direct path as the default for compatibility.
- Add configurable cube-router enablement and CIDR settings in one-click deploy.
- Preserve existing network policy, DNS allow-list, CubeEgress, and port mapping semantics.
- Add docs and examples for:
  - GRE remote as internet gateway
  - dual-NIC routing
- Regenerate CubeVS BPF objects for the final eBPF source.

## Notes

- Existing outbound connections may need to reconnect when cube-router is enabled for the first time.
- Port mapping remains bound to the primary NIC.
- The default behavior is unchanged unless cube-router is explicitly enabled.

## Testing

Tested route-aware egress with:
- GRE tunnel egress
- dual-NIC routing
- primary NIC egress
- existing port mapping path
- CubeEgress compatibility

BPF objects were regenerated after rebasing onto the latest open-source master.

@@ -0,0 +1,270 @@
+# Route-Aware Egress
+
+By default, CubeSandbox keeps the original egress behavior: CubeVS sends sandbox outbound packets directly to the node's primary network interface. This is simple and works well for single-NIC nodes, but it does not let the Linux routing table choose another egress device, such as a secondary NIC, GRE tunnel, VXLAN device, VPN interface, or policy-routed path.
+
+The optional **cube-router** mode changes only the host-side egress path. Sandbox network policy, DNS allow-list learning, CubeEgress L7 proxying, and port mapping keep their existing semantics.
+
+## When To Enable It
+
+Enable cube-router when sandbox traffic should follow host routing instead of always leaving from the primary NIC. Common cases include:
+
+- The node has multiple NICs and different destination CIDRs should leave through different interfaces.
+- Some destinations are reachable only through a tunnel device, such as GRE, VXLAN, WireGuard, or an internal VPN.
+- You need route-aware sandbox egress without changing the host's global default route.
+
+Keep it disabled when the primary NIC direct path is enough. The default is disabled for upgrade compatibility.
+
+## How It Works
+
+When cube-router is disabled, CubeVS performs the original direct SNAT path:
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+    sandbox[Sandbox] --> tap[TAP]
+    tap --> fromCube[CubeVS from_cube]
+    fromCube --> nic[Primary NIC]
+```
+
+When cube-router is enabled, CubeVS first normalizes outbound packets to an internal NAT IP, then injects them into an internal dummy device named `cube-router`. From there, the Linux kernel performs normal forwarding, conntrack, routing lookup, and final MASQUERADE:
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+    sandbox[Sandbox] --> tap[TAP]
+    tap --> fromCube[CubeVS from_cube]
+    fromCube --> router[cube-router]
+    router --> kernel[Linux routing table]
+    kernel --> egress[Selected egress device]
+```
+
+This means CubeSandbox does not need to understand every device type. If Linux can route traffic through that device, sandbox egress can use it.
+
+Port mapping remains bound to the node's primary NIC. It is not exposed on every possible egress device.
+
+## Enable During Installation
+
+Set these variables in `deploy/one-click/.env` before running the one-click installer or upgrade:
+
+```bash
+CUBE_SANDBOX_CUBE_ROUTER_ENABLE=1
+# Optional. Leave empty to derive addresses from CUBE_SANDBOX_NETWORK_CIDR.
+CUBE_SANDBOX_CUBE_ROUTER_CIDR=
+```
+
+If `CUBE_SANDBOX_CUBE_ROUTER_CIDR` is empty, CubeSandbox reserves the last two usable IPs from the sandbox CIDR. With the default sandbox CIDR `192.168.0.0/18`, this becomes:
+
+| Address | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `192.168.63.253/32` | `cube-router` device IP |
+| `192.168.63.254` | internal SNAT IP used before host routing |
+
+If you set a custom cube-router CIDR, it must be an aligned private IPv4 CIDR with a mask between `/16` and `/30`. CubeSandbox uses `.1` as the router IP and `.2` as the internal SNAT IP:
+
+```bash

+# Route-Aware Egress
+
+By default, CubeSandbox keeps the original egress behavior: CubeVS sends sandbox outbound packets directly to the node's primary network interface. This is simple and works well for single-NIC nodes, but it does not let the Linux routing table choose another egress device, such as a secondary NIC, GRE tunnel, VXLAN device, VPN interface, or policy-routed path.
+
+The optional **cube-router** mode changes only the host-side egress path. Sandbox network policy, DNS allow-list learning, CubeEgress L7 proxying, and port mapping keep their existing semantics.
+
+## When To Enable It
+
+Enable cube-router when sandbox traffic should follow host routing instead of always leaving from the primary NIC. Common cases include:
+
+- The node has multiple NICs and different destination CIDRs should leave through different interfaces.
+- Some destinations are reachable only through a tunnel device, such as GRE, VXLAN, WireGuard, or an internal VPN.
+- You need route-aware sandbox egress without changing the host's global default route.
+
+Keep it disabled when the primary NIC direct path is enough. The default is disabled for upgrade compatibility.
+
+## How It Works
+
+When cube-router is disabled, CubeVS performs the original direct SNAT path:
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+    sandbox[Sandbox] --> tap[TAP]
+    tap --> fromCube[CubeVS from_cube]
+    fromCube --> nic[Primary NIC]
+```
+
+When cube-router is enabled, CubeVS first normalizes outbound packets to an internal NAT IP, then injects them into an internal dummy device named `cube-router`. From there, the Linux kernel performs normal forwarding, conntrack, routing lookup, and final MASQUERADE:
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+    sandbox[Sandbox] --> tap[TAP]
+    tap --> fromCube[CubeVS from_cube]
+    fromCube --> router[cube-router]
+    router --> kernel[Linux routing table]
+    kernel --> egress[Selected egress device]
+```
+
+This means CubeSandbox does not need to understand every device type. If Linux can route traffic through that device, sandbox egress can use it.
+
+Port mapping remains bound to the node's primary NIC. It is not exposed on every possible egress device.
+
+## Enable During Installation
+
+Set these variables in `deploy/one-click/.env` before running the one-click installer or upgrade:
+
+```bash
+CUBE_SANDBOX_CUBE_ROUTER_ENABLE=1
+# Optional. Leave empty to derive addresses from CUBE_SANDBOX_NETWORK_CIDR.
+CUBE_SANDBOX_CUBE_ROUTER_CIDR=
+```

+If `CUBE_SANDBOX_CUBE_ROUTER_CIDR` is empty, CubeSandbox reserves the last two usable IPs from the sandbox CIDR. With the default sandbox CIDR `192.168.0.0/18`, this becomes:
+
+| Address | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `192.168.63.253/32` | `cube-router` device IP |
+| `192.168.63.254` | internal SNAT IP used before host routing |
+
+If you set a custom cube-router CIDR, it must be an aligned private IPv4 CIDR with a mask between `/16` and `/30`. CubeSandbox uses `.1` as the router IP and `.2` as the internal SNAT IP:

+```bash
+CUBE_SANDBOX_CUBE_ROUTER_ENABLE=1
+CUBE_SANDBOX_CUBE_ROUTER_CIDR=10.254.0.0/24
+```
+
+The custom CIDR must not overlap with existing host routes or interface addresses.
+

+ip addr show cube-router
+ip route | grep cube-router
+iptables -t nat -S POSTROUTING | grep MASQUERADE

## Summary

Adds the v0.5.0 changelog and updates the changelog index, mirroring the v0.4.0 entry layout. The body is written in the same style as the previous release notes: features grouped by audience, enhancements, bug fixes, documentation, and engineering improvements.

## What's in this PR

- `docs/changelog/v0.5.0.md` (new) — English release notes
- `docs/zh/changelog/v0.5.0.md` (new) — Chinese release notes
- `docs/changelog/index.md` — adds v0.5.0 row
- `docs/zh/changelog/index.md` — adds v0.5.0 row
- `docs/guide/digital-assistant.md` — fixes code-block language tag (`env` -> `bash`)
- `docs/zh/guide/digital-assistant.md` — same fix in Chinese

## Release scope

85 commits from 22 contributors since v0.4.0. Key themes:

- **Lifecycle**: e2b-compatible `lifecycle` kwarg with auto-pause/auto-resume, kill-on-timeout as the new default, `set_timeout` / `refresh` APIs, stable `end_at`
- **Network**: per-sandbox traffic access tokens, CubeEgress fail-closed bootstrap, CubeVS sandbox-to-host-service access, network hardening guide
- **Image and template**: pure-Go native rootfs export, TUI template management with pull progress, real envd version probing, fix for image-layer uid/gid squashing
- **Deployment**: `--mode upgrade` with three-way `.env` merge, external MySQL/Redis, Terraform-based Tencent Cloud cluster deployment, configurable TKE replicas
- **Control plane**: snapshot runtime binding rework fixing MySQL 1213 deadlocks under concurrent rollback, cross-replica node metadata sync, template-deletion resource cleanup paths

## Notes

This PR contains documentation only. The code changes corresponding to the listed features already landed on `master` since v0.4.0; the changelog is being published as a single release-note batch.

The two `digital-assistant.md` edits correct the fenced code-block language tag from `env` to `bash` so it renders correctly; no content change.

## Review: PR #707 — Integrate cube-egress into one-click runtime scripts

**Overall:** This is a well-structured PR that correctly integrates cube-egress into the one-click deployment scripts. The startup ordering (egress after cubelet/network-agent) and shutdown ordering (egress before cubelet) respect the dependency chain. The new scripts follow established patterns (`start_with_pidfile`, `stop_by_pidfile`, `require_root`, `|| true` guards) and use defense-in-depth correctly. Below are the noteworthy findings.

---

### 🔴 Security: Shell injection via `ENV_FILE` in `up-cube-egress.sh`

**File:** `deploy/one-click/scripts/one-click/up-cube-egress.sh:24`

`ENV_FILE` (derived from `ONE_CLICK_RUNTIME_ENV_FILE`) is interpolated unsanitized into a string passed to `bash -c`. An attacker who controls this env var can inject arbitrary shell commands as root. See the inline comment for details and suggested fix.

This follows a pre-existing pattern — other `start_with_pidfile` call sites in `up.sh` and `up-compute.sh` have the same risk with their env-var-sourced variables. A systemic fix in `start_with_pidfile` itself would address all callers at once.

---

### 🟡 Code quality: Duplicated `common.sh` with behavioral drift

**Files:**
- `deploy/one-click/scripts/one-click/common.sh`
- `deploy/one-click/scripts/systemd/common.sh`

Both files define the same utility functions (`wait_for_http`, `escape_sed`, `refresh_pidfile_from_pattern`, etc.) with meaningful differences:

- **`wait_for_http`** — the systemd version logs the failing URL, wait duration, and curl error on timeout. The one-click version does not, making timeouts harder to diagnose.
- **`escape_sed`** — the one-click version strips newlines/carriage returns and accepts an explicit delimiter. The systemd version is a simpler one-liner.
- **`refresh_pidfile_from_pattern`** — different argument signatures (`name, pattern, retries` vs `pid_file, pattern, retries`).

Both already source `../common/validation.sh`, so a precedent for sharing exists. Extracting the shared subset into a single file would prevent further divergence and make bug fixes propagate automatically.

---

### 🟡 Test coverage gap: No tests for the new scripts

The existing test suite under `deploy/one-click/tests/` has zero coverage for the new cube-egress scripts. The CI workflow (`terraform-validate.yml`) does not trigger on `deploy/one-click/scripts/**` changes, and the most relevant test file (`test_runtime_file_safety.sh`) is not executed in CI at all.

**Recommendations from the test coverage review:**

1. Add static contract assertions for cube-egress systemd unit wiring (prepare hooks, dependency order) into `test_runtime_file_safety.sh`, following the existing patterns.
2. Wire `test_runtime_file_safety.sh` into CI.
3. Extend CI path triggers to include `deploy/one-click/scripts/**`.
4. Add subshell-based behavior tests for the new scripts' failure modes (missing systemd scripts, missing `docker`, each sub-script failing).

---

### 🟡 Performance: Startup latency budget stacking

`up-cube-egress.sh` runs 4 sequential phases (prepare → net-start → start → postcheck) on the main startup path before `quickcheck.sh` runs. Worst-case budget exceeds 300 seconds:

| Phase | Worst-case budget |
|---|---|
| prepare (CA download + network-agent bootstrap wait) | ~120s |
| net-start (socket interface wait) | ~30s |
| start (docker pull + container start) | depends on image size |
| postcheck (container health + TCP + HTTP) | ~200s |

In practice this is far faster, but the stacked budget means one slow component delays the entire node. The 60-second network-agent bootstrap wait in the prepare step is partially redundant with the earlier `wait_for_http` on network-agent's `/readyz`.

Minor optimization: the two CA downloads in `cube-egress-prepare.sh` are independent and could be parallelized (`&`/`wait`) since the openssl verification block already acts as a synchronization barrier.

---

### 🟢 Documentation: Minor gaps

Both new scripts lack header comments explaining their purpose and architectural choices (e.g., why `cube-egress-net-start.sh` is called inline rather than as a separate systemd oneshot service). Adding a brief header to each would help future maintainers.

Existing Go source comments and the one-click README are accurate and up to date — no changes needed there.

---

### ✅ Positive highlights

- **Correct shutdown ordering:** egress stops before cubelet, with graceful container shutdown (`docker stop -t 15` before `stop_by_pidfile`), then network teardown
- **Defense-in-depth:** `|| true` guards in teardown handle partially-installed environments gracefully
- **Prerequisite validation:** all four systemd scripts are checked for existence and executability before startup
- **Consistent patterns:** `set -euo pipefail`, `require_root`, `require_cmd`, `test -x` guards used throughout
- **Robust resource cleanup:** PID files cleaned, container stop precedes network teardown, idempotent operations everywhere
<!-- cubesandbox-auto-review:end -->

**Security: `ENV_FILE` interpolated unsanitized into `bash -c` command string**

`start_with_pidfile` passes its second argument to `bash -c "${cmd}"`. Here `ENV_FILE` is embedded via shell interpolation into that command string. If `ONE_CLICK_RUNTIME_ENV_FILE` (the env var backing `ENV_FILE`) contains characters like `"`, `;`, backticks, or `$()`, an attacker can inject arbitrary shell commands that execute as root before the intended start script runs.

**Suggestion:** Validate `ENV_FILE` against a safe character set before use:
```bash
case "${ENV_FILE}" in
  *[!a-zA-Z0-9_./-]*)
    die "ENV_FILE contains unsafe characters: ${ENV_FILE}"
    ;;
esac
```

## Review: PR #706 — Webhook Delivery for Sandbox Lifecycle Events

Overall, this is a well-structured implementation with thorough tests for happy paths, solid SSRF guards at the URL validation layer, and careful secret redaction. Below are noteworthy issues organized by severity.

### 🔴 High Severity

**1. `response_body_summary` reads the body then discards it** (`CubeAPI/src/logging/http.rs:307-332`)

The function reads up to 2048 bytes from the error response but returns `<N response body bytes omitted>` instead of including the actual text. Every webhook delivery failure log reads like `webhook endpoint returned 500: <42 response body bytes omitted>`, giving operators zero diagnostic information. Fix: use `String::from_utf8_lossy(&body)`.

**2. DNS rebinding bypasses startup-only IP validation** (`CubeAPI/src/config/mod.rs:303-348`)

Hostnames are resolved to IPs and validated against the private-IP blocklist only at startup, but `reqwest` re-resolves at delivery time. An attacker controlling DNS for the webhook URL can serve a safe IP at startup and switch to a private/metadata IP by delivery time. Consider resolving+validating at delivery time, or pinning the resolved `SocketAddr`.

**3. No replay protection on signed payloads** (`CubeAPI/src/logging/http.rs:334-340`, `receiver.py:25-31`)

The HMAC covers only the request body. `X-Cube-Delivery` and the timestamp are not signed. An observer can replay the payload verbatim at any future time, and the example receiver has no delivery-ID tracking. Include the delivery ID in the HMAC input and recommend receivers enforce deduplication.

### 🟠 Medium Severity

**4. Two-tier silent event drops with no backpressure** (`CubeAPI/src/logging/http.rs:129-136`, `169-177`)

Events are silently dropped at two levels: `try_send` in `log()` (channel full), and `try_acquire_owned` in the worker (endpoint concurrency saturated). An operator's only indication is a `warn!` log. At minimum, document both drop paths in the webhooks doc. Consider using `send().await` for backpressure, or `acquire_owned().await` instead of `try_acquire_owned()` in the worker so queued events aren't wasted at the semaphore gate.

**5. Background worker panic silently kills all webhook delivery** (`CubeAPI/src/logging/http.rs:156-207`)

The `tokio::spawn` handle returned by `spawn_worker` is discarded. If the background task panics (e.g., from an `expect()` or unwrap), all webhook delivery stops silently. Events accumulate in the channel forever with no recovery. Consider at minimum logging on panic via a wrapper, or adding a supervision restart mechanism.

**6. Unnecessary `LogEvent` clone + repeated serialization per endpoint** (`CubeAPI/src/logging/http.rs:167`, `181`)

Each subscribed endpoint gets a deep-cloned `HashMap`. Plus, `deliver_once` serializes the event to JSON independently per endpoint even though the body is identical for endpoints without a secret. Consider serializing once and sharing the `Vec<u8>` body across endpoints.

**7. env var mutation races with parallel tests** (`CubeAPI/src/config/mod.rs:449-453`)

`std::env::set_var` mutates process-global state. Other tests running in parallel via `cargo test` (default) can see the poisoned value. Use a lock or refactor to inject env overrides as parameters.

**8. Webhook receiver startup message doesn't match behavior** (`receiver.py:102`)

Says "listening on .../webhook" but `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` dispatches all POST requests regardless of path — the handler never checks `self.path`. Either add path validation or correct the message.

### 🟡 Low Severity

- **No jitter in exponential backoff** (`http.rs:343-346`) — retries synchronize across endpoints.
- **`build_webhook_http_client` panics on failure** (`http.rs:29-33`) — could return `Result`.
- **`cfg.webhooks.clone()` at startup** (`main.rs:224`) — could use `std::mem::take`.
- **Backoff formula undocumented** (`docs/guide/webhooks.md:53`) — specify `initial * 2^(attempt-1)`.
- **Empty `events` → all events not documented** — code treats `"events": []` as subscribe-all, which is useful but not documented.

### ✅ What's Done Well

- Thorough SSRF protection in URL validation (scheme whitelist, IP blocklist, credentials rejection, redirect disabled).
- HMAC secret correctly redacted in `Debug` output on both config and runtime types, verified by tests.
- Timing-safe `compare_digest` in the Python receiver.
- Clean separation of hot path (`log()` → channel send) from background delivery with retry.
- Good test coverage for happy paths: delivery, HMAC signing, retries, concurrency isolation, redirect rejection, backoff arithmetic.
- Strong documentation with a runnable receiver example and accurate Chinese translation.

### 问题发现

1. **[高] DNS rebinding: 启动时校验的地址与实际请求时解析的地址可能不同**
   - 证据: `validate_webhook_hostname` 在配置加载阶段（`default_webhooks()` → `clean_webhook_endpoints`）用 `(host, port).to_socket_addrs()` 解析主机名并校验 IP 是否在允许范围内，但实际 HTTP 请求由 `reqwest::Client` 在 `deliver_once` 中发出，会**重新解析** DNS。攻击者控制的域名可以在校验通过后（例如启动时解析到 `1.2.3.4`）改变 DNS 记录，使运行期请求解析到 `169.254.169.254` 或内网地址，SSRF 防护被绕过。
   - 受影响调用方/流程: 所有使用主机名（而非 IP literal）配置的 webhook endpoint，尤其是长期运行的 CubeAPI 进程。
   - 最小可行修复: 在 `deliver_once` 发起请求前，对目标 URL 的解析结果做同样的 IP 校验（例如自定义 `reqwest::dns::Resolve` 实现，或在发送前手动 resolve + 校验 + 通过 IP 直连并设置 `Host` header），而不是只在配置加载时一次性校验。文档中提到"DNS check is a startup-time guard"承认了这个限制，但对于默认启用的安全特性，建议至少在 README/webhooks.md 中更明确地标注这是已知限制，或者实现请求时校验作为默认防护。

2. **[中] 配置解析失败时静默 fail-open，可能导致 webhook 静默失效或部分生效**
   - 证据: `CUBE_API_WEBHOOKS` JSON 解析失败时仅 `eprintln!` + `tracing::error!`，返回空列表（不是校验失败中止启动）；单个 endpoint URL 校验失败、重复 URL 也是静默跳过。这在配置错误时会导致运维认为 webhook 已配置生效，实际上部分或全部 endpoint 未加载，且没有任何强信号（如启动失败）暴露给部署方。
   - 受影响调用方/流程: 依赖 webhook 通知做审计、监控或自动化响应的下游系统。
   - 最小可行修复: 考虑区分"格式错误应阻止启动"与"单个 endpoint 无效应跳过"两类错误；至少确保这些警告级别日志在生产环境默认可见（当前 `tracing::warn`/`error` 依赖 `min_level` 配置，若 `LOG_LEVEL` 设置过高可能被过滤掉）。

3. **[中] `default_webhooks()` 在测试中修改全局环境变量,存在测试间竞态风险**
   - 证据: `env_parse_clamps_queue_capacity_to_effective_minimum` 测试用 `std::env::set_var`/`remove_var` 操作全局状态，Rust 测试默认并行执行，若同一 crate 内其他测试并发读取相关环境变量（如 `default_webhooks()` 依赖的 `CUBE_API_WEBHOOK_URLS` 等），存在数据竞争导致 flaky test 的风险。
   - 受影响调用方/流程: CI 测试稳定性。
   - 最小可行修复: 使用 `serial_test` crate 或等价机制串行化涉及环境变量的测试，或改为依赖注入而非直接读环境变量。

### 行级发现

- [CubeAPI/src/config/mod.rs:224] `default_webhooks()` 中 JSON 解析失败仅记录日志后返回空 `Vec::new()`（对应函数末尾的 fallback 路径），属于 fail-open；见 Finding 2，建议在文档或行为上明确这是有意设计还是应收紧。
- [CubeAPI/src/config/mod.rs:329] `validate_webhook_hostname` 依赖 `to_socket_addrs()` 做同步 DNS 解析，该调用是阻塞的，`default_webhooks()` 在 `ServerConfig::default()`（同步上下文）中被调用；虽然只在启动时执行一次可接受，但如果未来 DNS 解析变慢，会拖慢进程启动。可接受，仅供记录。
- [CubeAPI/src/config/mod.rs:301] `validate_webhook_url` 对 `http` + secret 组合只告警不阻止（scheme 检查在 293-296 行），与 Finding 1 的 rebinding 风险叠加时，HTTP 明文 + 可被 DNS rebinding 绕过的 SSRF 防护构成组合风险；建议至少在生产模式下考虑拒绝而非警告。
- [CubeAPI/src/logging/http.rs:349] `signature_header` 使用 `HmacSha256::new_from_slice` 对任意长度密钥没有强制最小长度校验，弱密钥（如空字符串会被上层 `filter(|s| !s.is_empty())` 挡掉，但极短密钥不受限）会削弱 HMAC 防护强度；非阻塞，可选加固。
- [CubeAPI/src/logging/http.rs:171] `try_send` 在队列满或 receiver 已关闭时静默丢弃事件并只记录 `warn`；这是有意为之的背压策略（避免阻塞主流程），设计合理，但建议在 `docs/guide/webhooks.md` 中已经提到"best-effort"，与实现一致，无需改动。

### Karpathy 评审

- 假设: 实现假设"启动时 DNS 校验 + IP 白名单"足以防御 SSRF；这在静态 IP 或短生命周期部署下成立，但对长期运行进程+动态域名场景不成立（rebinding）。文档中已诚实标注这一限制（`webhooks.md` 提到"DNS check is a startup-time guard"），说明作者已意识到该假设的边界，值得肯定，但作为默认安全特性建议进一步收紧或至少提升可见性。
- 简洁性: 整体实现克制，没有过度抽象。`EndpointWorker` + `Semaphore` per-endpoint 并发控制、`JoinSet` 管理投递任务的设计合理，没有引入不必要的通用层。
- 结构质量: `deliver_with_retries`/`deliver_once`/`response_body_summary` 职责清晰，`clean_webhook_endpoints` 把校验、去重、trim 逻辑集中在一处，符合 canonical ownership。未发现明显的结构退化或重复造轮子。
- 变更范围: 变更集中在新增能力（webhook 投递 + 配置 + 文档 + 示例），未见无关重构或格式噪声。`logging/mod.rs` 的 doc 表格更新准确反映了状态变化。
- 验证: 测试覆盖较全面——正常投递、HMAC 签名、重试、redirect 拒绝、per-endpoint 并发隔离（slow endpoint 不阻塞 fast endpoint）、配置校验（私网 IP、IPv4-mapped IPv6、重复 URL、无效 scheme）均有对应测试。缺口：没有针对 DNS rebinding 场景的测试（即启动校验通过后 DNS 记录变化的场景），也没有测试 webhook 配置解析失败时的进程行为（是否应该阻止启动）。

### 缺失覆盖

- 请求时（而非仅启动时）SSRF/rebinding 防护的测试或至少已知限制的显式验收。
- 私网 hostname（非 IP literal，如内部服务发现域名解析到私网地址）在 `validate_webhook_hostname` 路径下的负向测试用例（当前测试集中在 IP literal 校验，hostname 路径只有一个 loopback 正向用例）。
- 集成测试验证 `async_main` 中 webhook logger 只在 `cfg.webhooks` 非空时才被加入 `MultiLogger`（当前只有单元测试覆盖 `HttpLogger` 本身，未覆盖 wiring 逻辑）。
Refs #642

## Summary
- Add CubeAPI webhook delivery for sandbox lifecycle events (`sandbox.created`, `sandbox.deleted`, `sandbox.paused`, `sandbox.resumed`).
- Support JSON/env endpoint configuration, per-event subscriptions, async delivery queue, retry with exponential backoff, and optional HMAC-SHA256 signatures.
- Add runnable receiver example plus English/Chinese integration docs.

## Validation
- `cargo fmt --manifest-path CubeAPI/Cargo.toml -- --check`
- `cargo test --manifest-path CubeAPI/Cargo.toml`
- `npm run docs:build` from `docs/`
- `python3 -m py_compile examples/webhook-receiver/receiver.py`
- `git diff --check`

item.title: feat: issue-642

review_comments.body: **Worker JoinHandle not stored — no graceful shutdown path** — The `spawn_worker` JoinHandle at line 149 is discarded. During shutdown, the axum server stops, `flush()` drains pending deliveries, and then `HttpLogger` is dropped — but the worker task is cancelled by the runtime before its `drain_deliveries` on channel-close can complete. Storing the handle and awaiting it on shutdown would ensure all pending deliveries finish before the process exits.

**Empty event list silently subscribes to ALL events** — When the event filter cleanup removes all entries (e.g., user passes `"events": [""]`), the resulting empty `Vec` causes `endpoint_subscribes` (http.rs:202-208) to return `true` for every event. This silently converts an invalid config into an all-events subscription. A user with a typo or misplaced comma would unknowingly receive events they didn't intend to subscribe to.

**Fix:** Log a warning when cleaning removes all explicitly-provided events, so this behavior is at least observable.

**DNS hostname SSRF — no IP resolution validation** — When the webhook URL uses a DNS name rather than an IP literal, the code skips IP validation entirely (the `if let Ok(ip) = host.parse::<IpAddr>()` guard at line 295). A DNS name pointing at `metadata.google.internal` or `10.0.0.1.internal` passes validation despite resolving to a private IP.

**Fix:** Resolve DNS names at config time and validate all resolved addresses against the same IP blocklist. Note this requires making `validate_webhook_url` async (or using synchronous DNS).

**Unrestricted HTTP redirect policy** — `reqwest::Client::new()` defaults to following up to 10 cross-origin redirects. A compromised or malicious webhook endpoint could return a 302/307 redirect pointing at an internal service (e.g., cloud metadata API, internal Redis), and the CubeAPI server would follow it without validation.

**Fix:** Build the client with a restrictive redirect policy:

```rust
reqwest::Client::builder()
    .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none())
    .build()
    .expect("failed to build webhook HTTP client")
```

review_comments.body: **Defaulting to 0.0.0.0 exposes the receiver to all network interfaces.** This is the example receiver that users may deploy as-is. Combined with the optional nature of HMAC verification, this is a risk. Change the default to `127.0.0.1` and add a `Content-Length` cap (the current code reads however many bytes the header specifies).

review_comments.body: **Dead code.** `HttpLoggerConfig` and `HttpLogger::new()` are never used by the new webhook system — the only call site in `main.rs` uses `from_endpoints()`. The `batch_size` and `flush_interval_secs` fields are never read, but their names imply batching semantics that don't exist (events are forwarded one-at-a-time). Remove ~30 lines and the `#[allow(dead_code)]` annotation.

**Silent fallback on parse failure.** When an env var is present but unparseable (e.g., `CUBE_API_WEBHOOK_QUEUE_CAPACITY=not-a-number`), this returns the default with no warning. Operators won't know their config was ignored. Add a `warn!()` when the var exists but parsing fails.

**Silent error body read failure.** If `response.text()` fails (connection reset, encoding issue), its error is discarded and the logged error will say something like `"webhook endpoint returned 500: "` — losing diagnostic value. Log the read error before defaulting to empty string.

**Single worker is a throughput bottleneck.** This `spawn_worker` dequeues events one at a time, and `join_all` waits for all endpoint deliveries to complete before picking up the next event. A single slow endpoint (or one that hits the 5s timeout) stalls delivery to all other endpoints and accelerates queue filling. Consider per-endpoint channels or spawning independent per-endpoint tasks so slow deliveries don't cascade.

This match arm blocks the worker on per-endpoint retries/backoff (via `join_all(...).await`), so one slow/unreachable endpoint stalls queue draining and increases the likelihood of dropping subsequent events when the bounded channel fills. Consider decoupling delivery from the receive loop by spawning a per-event task and tracking join handles so `flush()` can still wait for in-flight work.

`CUBE_API_WEBHOOK_QUEUE_CAPACITY` can currently be set to 0, but the channel creation clamps it to at least 1 (`max(1)`). Clamping here makes the configuration and logs reflect the effective behavior.

Reading and embedding the entire non-2xx response body into the error message is unbounded (potential memory spike if the endpoint returns a large payload) and can also leak sensitive response data into logs. It’s safer to cap the logged body to a small preview (or omit it entirely).
